The district was created ahead of the [[1969 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1969 House elections]] after the former Mountain Province was divided into the provinces of [[Benguet]], [[Mountain Province]], [[Ifugao]], and [[Kalinga-Apayao]] in 1966.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=4695|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/7121 |title=An Act Creating the Provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Ifugao and Kalinga-Apayao|date=June 18, 1966|accessdate=July 14, 2026}} It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] since the [[7th Congress of the Philippines|7th Congress]] from 1969 to 1972, in the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]], the unicameral parliament that replaced the House of Representatives from 1984 to 1986, and in the restored House from the [[10th Congress of the Philippines|10th Congress]] onwards. The district served as an electoral district in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1971|1971 Constitutional Convention]], with two delegates representing Benguet at-large.{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/14108|chamber=RA|number=6132|date=August 24, 1970|title=An Act Implementing Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Two as Amended by Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Four of the Congress of the Philippines Calling for a Constitutional Convention, Providing for Proportional Representation Therein and Other Details Relating to the Election of Delegates to and the Holding of the Constitutional Convention, Repealing for the Purpose Republic Act Four Thousand Nine Hundred Fourteen, and for Other Purposes}} From 1987 to 1995, the district was designated as Benguet's 2nd congressional district, while [[Baguio|Baguio City]] constituted Benguet's 1st congressional district. In 1995, the 1st district was redesignated as [[Baguio's at-large congressional district]], and the 2nd district became Benguet's lone district.{{Cite web |title=Roster of Philippine Legislators (1907 - 2019) |url=https://docs.congress.hrep.online/download/docs/roster-legislators.pdf |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |page=59}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Eric Yap]] of [[Lakas–CMD]].{{Cite web |title=House Members - 20th Congress |url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/house-members |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]]}} == Recent election results from province-wide races == {| class="wikitable" !
